headline: A 2021 law extends federal medical malpractice protection to urban Indian organizations and their employees by treating them as part of the Public Health Service.
what_it_does: The law treats urban Indian organizations and their employees as part of the Public Health Service for certain personal injury claims. This gives them federal tort claim coverage, which is medical malpractice liability protection. Before this law, that coverage applied to Indian tribes, tribal organizations, Indian contractors, and their employees.

who_it_affects.how: They are now covered by federal medical malpractice liability protection through the Public Health Service, the same coverage previously available to tribes and tribal organizations.
Their personal injury claims tied to covered work can fall under the same federal liability protection that applies to Public Health Service staff.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on January 5, 2021.
